newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania swings to $22.2 mln trade deficit in April.
newsitem.headline: Romania swings to $22.2 mln trade deficit in April.

text.p: Romania's trade balance switched to a $22.2 million deficit in April from a $12.9 million surplus in March, the National Statistics Board (CNS) said on Friday.
A CNS report said exports had seen a 2.4 percent fall to $676.3 million in April from the previous month, while imports had been 2.7 percent up at $698.5 million.
It said exports fell by 0.7 percent to $2.62 billion over January-April from the equivalent period of 1996, with textiles and steel products topping the list.

Four-month imports dropped by 12.3 percent from the year-ago period, narrowing the trade deficit to $229.6 million in the first four months from $609.7 million in the same period of 1996, the report said.

The private sector accounted for 53.3 percent of exports and 47.7 percent of imports over January-April. Italy was the leading importer of Romanian goods while Germany was the source of half of Romanian imports.

NOTES -- Previous data in brackets. All figures FOB. The CNS said four-month imports this year included $87.9 million worth of oil imports on which customs documents were delayed. The 1997 data are subject to revisions.
